Equal Earth vs. Mercator: Cartographic Distortion & Projection Analysis¶

A Geospatial Comparative Analysis of World Map Projections and Area Representation¶

Same planet, a very different way of seeing it, breaking down the cartographic shift from Mercator to Equal Earth 🌍📐

¶

Author: Imtiaj Iqbal Mahfuj

📝 Overview¶

This project explores spatial patterns, integrates remote sensing datasets, and applies geospatial Python tools to visualize and analyze global cartographic projection distortion between the standard Mercator projection and the Equal Earth projection. It aims to uncover key insights that support data-driven decision-making for cartographic communication, education, and global thematic mapping.

The standard Mercator projection (EPSG:3395), designed in 1569 for nautical navigation, preserves local conformal shapes and rhumb lines at the expense of extreme areal distortion toward the poles. This creates significant misrepresentations of landmasses, vastly exaggerating regions like Greenland, North America, and Eurasia relative to equatorial continents such as Africa and South America. The Equal Earth projection (EPSG:8857), created in 2018 and formally adopted by international organizations including the United Nations, addresses this distortion by providing an equal-area, visually balanced representation that accurately preserves relative continent sizes without drastic shape distortion.

This work directly benefits cartographers, urban and regional planners, GIS educators, researchers, and policy analysts who require unbiased global baseline visualizations. By deploying custom Python automated workflows with GeoPandas and Matplotlib, this repository reproduces, benchmarks, and generates high-impact editorial graphics comparing both projections across multiple multi-platform aspect ratios.

🛠️ Tools & Technologies¶

⚙️ Methodology¶

Step Description
1. Data Collection Programmatic download of Natural Earth Cultural Vectors (1:110m Admin-0 Countries dataset) with automated fallback mirrors and integrity verification.
2. Preprocessing Coordinate Reference System (CRS) transformation to Equal Earth (EPSG:8857) and spatial bounding-box clipping (box(-180, -59, 180, 84)) prior to projecting to World Mercator (EPSG:3395) to prevent polar asymptotic singularity.
3. Analysis Geometry densification along longitudes and latitudes to construct smooth, curved graticules (30° intervals) and global geodesic boundary lines under non-linear projection transforms.
4. Visualization Publication-grade editorial styling using dark-mode aesthetics (obsidian #141413, marigold #E08838, taupe #423E3B), automated card typography chips, and multi-format exports (1920x1080, 1080x1350, 1280x720).

2. Prepare the two projections¶

In [59]:
# Equal Earth: everything
world_ee = world.to_crs(EQUAL_EARTH)

# Mercator: clip out the poles / Antarctica first (in lon-lat), then project
world_merc = gpd.clip(world, box(-180, -59, 180, 84)).to_crs(MERCATOR)


def graticule(lon_step=30, lat_step=30, lat_min=-90, lat_max=90):
    """Graticule as a lon/lat GeoSeries, densified so it curves when projected."""
    lines = []
    lats = np.linspace(lat_min, lat_max, 181)
    for lon in range(-180, 181, lon_step):
        lines.append(LineString(np.column_stack([np.full_like(lats, float(lon)), lats])))
    lons = np.linspace(-180, 180, 361)
    for lat in range(-90, 91, lat_step):
        if lat_min <= lat <= lat_max:
            lines.append(LineString(np.column_stack([lons, np.full_like(lons, float(lat))])))
    return gpd.GeoSeries(lines, crs=4326)


def world_outline():
    """Outline of the whole globe (becomes the curved Equal Earth border)."""
    top    = [(x,  90.0) for x in np.linspace(-180, 180, 361)]
    right  = [(180.0,  y) for y in np.linspace(90, -90, 181)]
    bottom = [(x, -90.0) for x in np.linspace(180, -180, 361)]
    left   = [(-180.0, y) for y in np.linspace(-90, 90, 181)]
    return gpd.GeoSeries([LineString(top + right + bottom + left)], crs=4326)


grat_ee    = graticule().to_crs(EQUAL_EARTH)
border_ee  = world_outline().to_crs(EQUAL_EARTH)
grat_merc  = graticule(lat_min=-59, lat_max=84).to_crs(MERCATOR)
border_merc = gpd.GeoSeries([box(-180, -59, 180, 84).boundary], crs=4326).to_crs(MERCATOR)


def draw_map(ax, land, grat, border, land_color):
    grat.plot(ax=ax, color=GRAT, linewidth=0.7, zorder=1)
    land.plot(ax=ax, color=land_color, edgecolor=BG, linewidth=0.35, zorder=2)
    border.plot(ax=ax, color=EDGE, linewidth=1.0, zorder=3)
    ax.set_aspect("equal")
    ax.axis("off")


def chip(fig, x, y, text, size=20, ha="left"):
    fig.text(x, y, text, fontsize=size, fontweight="bold", color="#CFCFCF",
             ha=ha, va="center",
             bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.45", facecolor=CHIP_BG,
                       edgecolor=CHIP_EDGE, linewidth=1.2))


def headline(fig, y1, y2, size, x=0.5):
    fig.text(x, y1, "THE UN VOTED TO CHANGE", fontsize=size, fontfamily=HEADLINE_FONT,
             color=TEXT, ha="center", va="center")
    fig.text(x, y2, "THE WORLD MAP", fontsize=size * 1.12, fontfamily=HEADLINE_FONT,
             color=MAGENTA, ha="center", va="center")


# VOTE = "164 in favour  \u00b7  6 abstentions  \u00b7  1 against \u2014 the United States"
# CREDIT = "Data: Natural Earth"

📊 Results & Insights¶

  • 🔹 True Continental Scale: In the Equal Earth projection, Africa's true land area (~30.37 million km²) is faithfully represented as roughly 14 times larger than Greenland (~2.16 million km²), dispelling the visual parity falsely suggested by Mercator maps.
  • 🔹 Boundary and Polar Behavior: Mercator maps inherently fail at extreme latitudes, requiring artificial truncation at ~84°N and ~59°S, whereas Equal Earth encapsulates the entire globe and polar caps seamlessly within a curved pseudocylindrical bounding perimeter.
  • 🔹 Editorial Cartography Benchmarks: Successfully exported automated layouts across 16:9 desktop presentations, 4:5 vertical LinkedIn feeds, and YouTube 720p thumbnails without manual graphic design intervention.

❓ Why this project?¶

  • Addresses the persistent public misconception of global landmass sizes caused by centuries of overreliance on conformal Mercator wall maps.
  • Bridges the gap between programmatic GIS pipelines and high-end visual journalism, demonstrating that publication-quality cartographic infographics can be completely automated with open-source Python libraries.
  • Supports ethical and objective cartographic standards in line with international bodies such as the UN and academic research institutions.

✨ Features¶

  • Fully automated vector pipeline downloading and caching 1:110m Natural Earth datasets
  • Programmatic graticule generation with dynamic line-densification for smooth projection re-projection
  • Custom high-contrast dark theme optimized for technical publications and social media reach
  • Multi-resolution layout engine supporting 1080p, YouTube 720p thumbnails, and LinkedIn vertical graphics (1080x1350)
  • Exportable maps/plots (PNG, SVG, GeoTIFF)
  • Notebook-ready examples (Jupyter / Colab)
